source.title: Time Matters in Regularizing Deep Networks: Weight Decay and Data Augmentation Affect Early Learning Dynamics, Matter Little Near Convergence
source.authors: Aditya Golatkar; Alessandro Achille; Stefano Soatto

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how timing weight decay and data augmentation affect held-out generalization, using training interventions and Fisher-information measurements rather than the original claim’s tests of memorization capacity, width, or sharpness.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test fitting random labels, capacity beyond interpolation, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, or memorized-example removal. Its own regularization-timing results, test accuracies, and Fisher-information associations bear on V6’s generalization question and V7’s trained-network-measurement question. The L2 norm is discussed as a correlate but does not get a row because no distinct outcome measure relating it to the generalization gap is reported. Cited prior findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures the timing of weight decay and data augmentation, Fisher trace, and effective learning rate. It does not test any listed version: V6 requires dropout comparisons or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation; V7 specifies magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, which Fisher trace does not measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation: early regularization influences training trajectories and final generalization, while changing regularization later can move the final weights without improving accuracy. Qualify the timing summary: weight decay shows stronger early sensitivity, augmentation can matter during intermediate epochs, and constant-learning-rate experiments are inconclusive. The proposed mechanism is an interpretation rather than a demonstrated causal account.
record.recipe_differences: Uses controlled timing changes to weight decay and data augmentation, then reports test accuracy and Fisher-information associations; it does not perform the claim versions’ capacity, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or perturbation-sharpness tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies with regularizer (weight decay versus data augmentation), timing, architecture, dataset, batch normalization, and learning-rate schedule. Constant learning-rate experiments are explicitly inconclusive.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuing weight decay or augmentation beyond an initial period gives little additional benefit; delaying their onset can impair final accuracy. ResNet-18 test error rises from 5% to 7% when weight decay begins at epoch 50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization benefit of weight decay and data augmentation depends on when they are applied, with timing effects varying across regularizers and training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-decay windows starting at epochs 0, 25, and 50 increase test accuracy by 1.92%, 1.39%, and 0.24%, respectively. Augmentation has a less concentrated sensitivity pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early training is especially sensitive to weight decay; augmentation can benefit a broader portion of training.

fits_no_version.finding: Peak Fisher trace correlates with final test accuracy at r=0.92 (p<0.001), whereas final trace has r=0.29 (p>0.05), among ResNet-18 models achieving 100% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transient Fisher curvature can predict generalization better than final Fisher curvature in weight-decay timing experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean initial and final effective learning rates correlate with test accuracy at r=0.96 and r=0.85, respectively, both p<0.001.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial effective learning rate correlates more strongly with generalization than final effective learning rate in these experiments.

record.problems: The authors state that their exploration is not exhaustive. Main results use two datasets and two architectures; constant-learning-rate results are inconclusive. Several per-epoch values are presented only in figures, and uncertainty is reported as thrice the standard deviation across five trials for Figure 1.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure-only epoch-specific values were not reconstructed as numeric values; the text-described aggregate patterns and explicitly stated numeric comparisons were recorded.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Generalization as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons, tuning, and recovery strategies.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

All parts: dropout is not varied; neither dropout dosage nor small-data effects nor joint removal of dropout and weight decay is tested. All-CNN explicitly uses batch normalization instead of dropout.
All parts: magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures are not measured.
Identifying and removing memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions because their measures do not operationalize those versions. This does not negate the reported timing effects or correlations. No additional results bearing on a listed version were identified in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning.
Dropout, very small training sets, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining after identifying memorized examples.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained for 200 epochs; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Weight decay was used until the stated epoch, then removed; final test accuracy reported by removal epoch.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy / generalization after early termination of regularization
rows.baseline: Regularizing throughout training; figure gives this as a dashed line, exact value not stated for this row.
rows.value: Applying regularization beyond the initial transient (around 100 epochs) produces no measurable improvement in generalization; early removal at epoch 75 is not numerically stated for ResNet-18.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate thrice the standard deviation across 5 independent trials (Figure 1).
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative result; precise accuracy values for individual removal epochs are not stated.
rows.check: Weight-decay timing does not test V6. The reported lack of benefit from continuing weight decay is a valid timing result. Figure 3 concerns CIFAR-100, not this row's CIFAR-10 condition.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.stage_stated: trained for 200 epochs; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Weight decay was used until the stated epoch, then removed; final test accuracy reported by removal epoch.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy / generalization after early termination of regularization
rows.baseline: Regularizing throughout training; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Early removal of regularization at epoch 75 actually improves generalization; exact accuracy difference not stated.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate thrice the standard deviation across 5 independent trials (Figure 1).
rows.note: The paper gives a qualitative improvement but does not state the numeric value.
rows.check: No dropout comparison or joint removal is performed. The Figure 1 caption identifies improved All-CNN generalization after removal at epoch 75 but does not explicitly identify the regularizer; assigning that statement specifically to weight decay requires inspecting the plotted curve.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained for 200 epochs, with an additional 50 epochs for late regularization onset; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Weight decay was turned on at the stated epoch and applied through convergence.
rows.baseline: 5% test error when regularizing all along.
rows.value: 7% test error with onset at epoch 50; the text calls this a 40% increase in test error.
rows.note: This is a direct numeric comparison of delayed versus continuous weight decay.
rows.check: The 5% versus 7% test-error comparison measures delayed weight decay, not dropout. It cannot establish a reversed dropout effect. The extra 50 training epochs apply to onset at epochs 150/175, not this epoch-50 condition.

rows.baseline: Data augmentation throughout training; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Adding a regularizer after the initial transient yields no benefit; exact value not stated for this condition.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate thrice the standard deviation across 5 independent trials (Figure 1).
rows.note: The text gives the general finding for delayed regularization; separate values by onset epoch are figure-only.
rows.check: Delayed augmentation does not test V6. The stated absence of late benefit is relative to training without augmentation, rather than equality with augmentation throughout. Figure 3 concerns CIFAR-100.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained for 200 epochs; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Weight decay applied during a 50-epoch sliding window; sensitivity reported relative to unregularized training.
rows.measure: Mean test accuracy increase relative to unregularized training
rows.baseline: Unregularized training; reference is a relative increase.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate thrice the standard deviation across 5 independent trials (Figure 1).
rows.locator: Section 4, Sliding Window Regularization; Figure 9 caption
rows.note: The paper reports this numeric value for the weight-decay window beginning at epoch 0.
rows.check: The 1.92% accuracy increase measures a weight-decay window, not dropout. The reference omits weight decay but retains data augmentation; it is not wholly unregularized training.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained for 200 epochs; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Data augmentation applied during a 50-epoch sliding window; sensitivity measured relative to unregularized training.
rows.measure: Sensitivity, change in final accuracy relative to unregularized training
rows.baseline: Unregularized training; exact numeric value for a specified window is figure-only.
rows.value: Data augmentation has essentially the same effect throughout training.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate thrice the standard deviation across 5 independent trials (Figure 1).
rows.note: The text describes the sensitivity pattern but does not provide separate numbers for each window onset.
rows.check: The augmentation-window sensitivity pattern does not test V6. The baseline retains weight decay. Similar effects across window positions do not themselves imply an incomplete regularization benefit.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained without batch normalization; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Weight decay was turned off after the stated epoch; final test accuracy reported by removal epoch.
rows.baseline: Weight decay throughout training; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Results are largely compatible with earlier experiments; removing weight decay right after the initial critical period surprisingly improves generalization.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars not stated in the Figure 4 text.
rows.check: Improvement after removing weight decay without batch normalization does not test dropout or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained without batch normalization; SGD with momentum 0.9
rows.operation_detail: Data augmentation was turned off after the stated epoch; final test accuracy reported by removal epoch.
rows.baseline: Data augmentation throughout training; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Results are largely compatible with earlier experiments; no precise per-epoch values stated.
rows.note: The text says timing effects remain and data augmentation shows a more marked dependency on timing in this setting.
rows.check: Augmentation timing without batch normalization does not test V6. The aggregate description also supplies no particular removal epoch or corresponding accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured peak Fisher Information Matrix trace and compared it with final test accuracy across trained networks.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between peak Fisher trace and final test accuracy
rows.uncertainty: p-values stated; no confidence interval stated.
rows.locator: Figure 5 caption; Section 4, Weight decay, Fisher and flatness
rows.note: The authors report that the peak value correlates far better with generalization than the final value. This measures Fisher trace, not magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness.
rows.check: Peak Fisher trace correlates with test accuracy at r=0.92, but it measures transient curvature rather than V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured final Fisher Information Matrix trace and compared it with final test accuracy across trained networks.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between final Fisher trace and final test accuracy
rows.uncertainty: p-values stated; no confidence interval stated.
rows.locator: Figure 5 caption; Section 4, Weight decay, Fisher and flatness
rows.note: The final trace is described as not correlating significantly with test accuracy; it is related to local curvature, not the specific magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: Final Fisher trace has a nonsignificant correlation of r=0.29 with test accuracy. This is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7, so its failure cannot establish absence of V7's effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
